Through this collaboration, the 41-year-old athlete will highlight stories of ambition and success during his global marathon tours, aiming to inspire future generations and encourage them to push beyond their limits.- Advertisement - Kipchoge ran his third of the seven World Tour marathons with a course record last Sunday in Melbourne, Australia.

body: Double Olympic marathon champion Eliud Kipchoge has signed a three-year deal as Absa Bank Kenya’s official World Tour Financial Partner. Through this collaboration, the 41-year-old athlete will highlight stories of ambition and success during his global marathon tours, aiming to inspire future generations and encourage them to push beyond their limits.- Advertisement - Kipchoge ran his third of the seven World Tour marathons with a course record last Sunday in Melbourne, Australia.

The five-time Berlin marathon champion began his inspirational runs on May 24th this year, finishing 16th at the Cape Town marathon in South Africa. He later achieved 12th position on July 13th at the Porto Alegre marathon in Brazil, on the South American continent.

Last Sunday’s victory was his first at the Melbourne Marathon, setting a new course record of 2:09:10. For Absa, that philosophy aligns closely with its commitment to helping customers realise ambitions that may once have seemed beyond reach, whether buying a home, starting a business, funding an education, growing wealth, or creating opportunities for future generations.

Beyond sports, Kipchoge is passionate about inspiring young people, promoting healthy living, and creating opportunities for communities to thrive. These priorities align strongly with Absa’s commitment to youth development, entrepreneurship, education, and meaningful community impact across the continent.

Yusuf Omari, Managing Director and CEO of Absa Bank Kenya, said, “Eliud Kipchoge’s achievements extend beyond sport. He embodies possibility beyond limits. He is proof of what is possible when talent, discipline, and purpose come together.
As a proudly Pan-African organisation, we are inspired by his journey in athletics, from his early cross-country trials in Kenya to becoming one of the most decorated athletes in the world.

articles.headline: Court of Appeal Allows Kenya-U.S. Health Deal Implementation Pending Appeal
articles.dek: The Court of Appeal has lifted High Court orders blocking a health cooperation framework between Kenya and the United States, citing public interest in maintaining essential healthcare services.
articles.lead: The Court of Appeal has cleared the way for the implementation of a health cooperation framework between Kenya and the United States, overturning High Court orders that had halted the program. A three-judge bench ruled that the public interest in continuing essential healthcare services outweighs the risks of proceeding with the agreement while a legal challenge is ongoing.
articles.takeaway: The Court of Appeal has lifted High Court orders blocking a health cooperation framework between Kenya and the United States, citing public interest in maintaining essential healthcare services.
body: The Court of Appeal has cleared the way for the implementation of a health cooperation framework between Kenya and the United States, overturning High Court orders that had halted the program. A three-judge bench ruled that the public interest in continuing essential healthcare services outweighs the risks of proceeding with the agreement while a legal challenge is ongoing.

The judges warned that suspending the framework could disrupt critical services, including treatment for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and immunization programs. They noted that the lives of citizens dependent on these treatments could be irreversibly impacted.

The framework, signed on December 4, 2025, is linked to the provision of essential medicines and healthcare support for millions of Kenyans. The government had argued that blocking the agreement threatened programs serving approximately 1.4 million Kenyans and could lead to drug resistance and broader public health risks.

Constitutional activist Okiya Omtatah Okoiti and the Katiba Institute had opposed the framework, raising concerns about data protection, privacy, public finance, devolution, and parliamentary oversight. These constitutional questions remain unresolved.

The appellate court's decision allows the government to proceed with the health cooperation program while the substantive legal dispute continues. The court emphasized that the framework had not been declared unconstitutional and that its decision focused on whether the implementation should be blocked pending the appeal.

articles.headline: Kenya's Economy Expands by Ksh 504 Billion in Six Months
articles.dek: The International Monetary Fund reports Kenya's GDP grew by approximately Ksh 504 billion between April and October 2026, maintaining its lead in Eastern Africa.
articles.lead: Kenya's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by USD 3.89 billion, equivalent to approximately Ksh 504 billion, over a six-month period from April to October 2026. During this time, the nation's GDP rose from USD 147.26 billion to USD 151.15 billion.
articles.takeaway: The International Monetary Fund reports Kenya's GDP grew by approximately Ksh 504 billion between April and October 2026, maintaining its lead in Eastern Africa.
body: Kenya's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by USD 3.89 billion, equivalent to approximately Ksh 504 billion, over a six-month period from April to October 2026. During this time, the nation's GDP rose from USD 147.26 billion to USD 151.15 billion.

Despite this growth, Kenya did not regain its former position as Africa's sixth-largest economy. However, it continues to hold the top economic ranking within Eastern Africa, with a GDP of USD 151.15 billion.

Neighboring economies showed mixed performance. Ethiopia's GDP grew by USD 6.15 billion (Ksh 797.84 billion) to reach USD 127.15 billion, securing the second spot in the region. Tanzania also saw growth, adding USD 1.29 billion (Ksh 167.35 billion) to its GDP.

In contrast, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda experienced contractions in their GDP. The DRC's GDP decreased by USD 1.12 billion (Ksh 145.30 billion), while Uganda's GDP fell by USD 1.13 billion (Ksh 146.59 billion).

On a continental scale, South Africa remains the largest economy, followed by Egypt and Nigeria. Kenya ranks seventh among Africa's largest economies, with the DRC, Ethiopia, and Ghana completing the top ten.

body: Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has emphasized the importance of accelerated infrastructure development in Kenya's Kerio Valley as a strategy to enhance security and create economic opportunities. Murkomen stated that sustained investment in roads and electricity is crucial for consolidating security gains and providing tangible benefits to local communities.

These development projects are intended to complement ongoing security operations, particularly in areas where residents have actively cooperated with the government to address banditry and cattle rustling. Murkomen highlighted this approach during the launch of the Kipsaraman-Kinyach Road and the Baringo North Last Mile Electricity Connectivity Project.

The Cabinet Secretary commended President William Ruto for directing the National Security Council to prioritize development in communities that have ceased criminal activities. He acknowledged the cooperation of local leaders and residents with security agencies in improving stability and addressing the proliferation of illegal firearms in the Kerio Valley.

Murkomen asserted that achieving sustainable peace in the region requires the government to translate security improvements into concrete development projects that enhance livelihoods and support economic activity. He described infrastructure investment as a critical component in addressing the root causes of banditry in the Kerio Valley.

The government's approach combines security measures with infrastructure investment and improved access to essential services. This strategy aims to strengthen cooperation between residents and security agencies, thereby fostering conditions for lasting peace and economic development in the affected region.

articles.dek: The new center will train public servants in AI, cybersecurity, and crisis management, aiming to enhance governance across Kenya and Africa.
articles.lead: The Kenya School of Government (KSG) is set to launch the Raila Amolo Odinga Regional Leadership and Governance Academy, a new institution dedicated to training public servants. The academy will focus on critical areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital leadership, and crisis management.
articles.takeaway: The new center will train public servants in AI, cybersecurity, and crisis management, aiming to enhance governance across Kenya and Africa.
body: The Kenya School of Government (KSG) is set to launch the Raila Amolo Odinga Regional Leadership and Governance Academy, a new institution dedicated to training public servants. The academy will focus on critical areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital leadership, and crisis management.

Established in honor of the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga, the center aims to equip leaders from Kenya and the wider African continent with the skills needed to address complex public administration challenges. This will be achieved through executive education, strategic planning, and policy research.

The academy's curriculum will incorporate a Leadership Simulation Laboratory that uses AI and interactive tools for real-time scenario testing. This lab is designed to prepare public officers for high-pressure situations, including economic shocks, climate emergencies, and public unrest.

Additionally, a Leadership Competency Framework, developed with the Public Service Commission, will utilize psychometric tests and other assessments to inform recruitment and promotion processes. A Policy and Strategic Foresight Hub will conduct scenario planning and publish policy recommendations for various government branches.

The academy also plans community outreach programs, mental health support for public servants, and preservation facilities, including a library and a museum dedicated to public service history. The Chandaria Innovation Hub will foster youth-focused initiatives and creativity.

articles.dek: Commemorations include dialogues, blood donation, and a candle-lighting ceremony to honor the former Prime Minister's legacy.
articles.lead: A series of events are being held from October 13 to 15 to mark the first anniversary of the death of former Prime Minister Raila Odinga. The commemorative activities are scheduled to take place in Kisumu, Kang'o ka Jaramogi, and Bondo.
articles.takeaway: Commemorations include dialogues, blood donation, and a candle-lighting ceremony to honor the former Prime Minister's legacy.
body: A series of events are being held from October 13 to 15 to mark the first anniversary of the death of former Prime Minister Raila Odinga. The commemorative activities are scheduled to take place in Kisumu, Kang'o ka Jaramogi, and Bondo.

The program, organized by the Raila Odinga Memorial Committee, aims to bring together family, community representatives, leaders, and the public to reflect on Odinga's life and contributions to Kenya's development and public service. Committee chairperson Adams Oloo described the week as one of gratitude and a moment to honor a legacy that continues to shape the nation.

Events began in Kisumu with an intergenerational dialogue focusing on social, political, and economic issues, intended to foster discussion among elders, youth, women, and religious leaders. A blood donation drive, symbolizing Odinga's spirit of selflessness, is also part of the activities.

On the evening of October 14, a candle-lighting ceremony will be held at Kang'o ka Jaramogi, led by Mama Ida Odinga. The committee encouraged Kenyans and friends of Raila Odinga worldwide to participate by lighting a candle in remembrance.

The main anniversary ceremony is scheduled for October 15 at Migwena Cultural Grounds in Bondo. Family members, leaders, and the public are expected to gather for this final event, which Oloo stated is a chance to recommit to the values and ideals of Odinga's public service.

articles.lead: Nairobi Woman Representative Esther Passaris has issued a direct warning to Governor Johnson Sakaja, signaling her potential entry into the 2027 Nairobi gubernatorial contest. Passaris urged Sakaja to improve his administration's performance, stating she would enter the race if she believes the county's top seat is at risk of falling to the opposition.
articles.takeaway: Nairobi Woman Representative Esther Passaris has put Governor Johnson Sakaja on notice, stating she may enter the 2027 gubernatorial race if the current administration's performance falters.
body: Nairobi Woman Representative Esther Passaris has issued a direct warning to Governor Johnson Sakaja, signaling her potential entry into the 2027 Nairobi gubernatorial contest. Passaris urged Sakaja to improve his administration's performance, stating she would enter the race if she believes the county's top seat is at risk of falling to the opposition.

"I want to put Sakaja on notice. Governor Sakaja, notice. If you do not style up and shape up and we see that we’re going to lose that seat, then Mimi Nitaingia, the race ya governor wa Nairobi," Passaris said during a women's retreat on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.

Passaris emphasized that Nairobi residents need tangible governance outcomes, not just rhetoric. She linked some of Nairobi's governance challenges to a deficit in women's elective leadership. Passaris noted that the number of elected women Members of County Assembly in Nairobi decreased from five in 2017 to four in 2022. Additionally, only one woman has been elected to represent Nairobi's 17 parliamentary constituencies in both the 2017 and 2022 General Elections.

Passaris's potential gubernatorial bid represents a shift in her political strategy for the 2027 elections. She had previously considered running for the Makadara parliamentary seat and then decided to defend her current position as Woman Representative before these latest remarks.

articles.dek: Nairobi — President William Ruto has announced a Sh20 billion road construction programme in Nandi County, targeting 350 kilometres of roads to improve transport and help farmers access markets. During a development tou…

articles.takeaway: Nairobi — President William Ruto has announced a Sh20 billion road construction programme in Nandi County, targeting 350 kilometres of roads to improve transport and help farmers access markets.
body: Nairobi — President William Ruto has announced a Sh20 billion road construction programme in Nandi County, targeting 350 kilometres of roads to improve transport and help farmers access markets.

During a development tour of the county, Ruto inspected the 24-kilometre Maraba-Kebeneti and Timboroa-Kopere roads in Tinderet Constituency. He also broke ground for the construction of the 17-kilometre Labuiywo-Kapkoros-Koisagat road, which will cost Sh1.3 billion.

Ruto said the visit was focused on development projects rather than politics. "Politics is still ahead of us. For now, we are focusing on development. I have come here to address roads, hospitals, markets and electricity," he said.

The road projects are expected to improve the movement of agricultural produce, connect rural communities to markets and ease access to essential services. The Labuiywo-Kapkoros-Koisagat road is also expected to improve links with Nandi Hills and neighbouring counties, including Uasin Gishu, Elgeyo Marakwet and West Pokot.

articles.dek: Spokesperson Charles Owino states all legitimate claims for land designated for the East Africa Oil Refinery in Lamu have been settled, dismissing current protests as based on fraudulent documents.
articles.lead: Government Spokesperson Charles Owino has dismissed claims of outstanding land compensation for the East Africa Oil Refinery project in Lamu. He asserted on Monday, October 12, 2026, that the government has already compensated and relocated all legitimate occupants of the land.
articles.takeaway: Spokesperson Charles Owino states all legitimate claims for land designated for the East Africa Oil Refinery in Lamu have been settled, dismissing current protests as based on fraudulent documents.
body: Government Spokesperson Charles Owino has dismissed claims of outstanding land compensation for the East Africa Oil Refinery project in Lamu. He asserted on Monday, October 12, 2026, that the government has already compensated and relocated all legitimate occupants of the land.

Protests reportedly erupted after the project's groundbreaking ceremony, with some individuals claiming they had not been paid for their land. Owino clarified that approximately 28,199 hectares were allocated to the Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) for port infrastructure development.

He explained that the National Land Commission (NLC) received KSh 1.4 billion from KPA to compensate around 90 families who originally occupied the land. The land titles, however, remain registered under the LAPSSET Corridor project.

Owino stated that any individuals presenting title deeds now are relying on fraudulent documents, as the judiciary has ruled on ownership disputes. He added that ongoing investigations will address any irregularities that occurred during the property's management under LAPSSET.

In separate remarks, Owino refuted claims that an imported Ebola case was being used to solicit external funding, urging against the politicization of public health measures. He also announced that Mashujaa Day celebrations will be held at Kipchoge Keino Stadium in Eldoret on October 20, 2026, jointly hosted by Uasin Gishu, Nandi, and Elgeyo Marakwet counties.

(Xinhua/Michael Tewelde) NAIROBI, Kenya, Oct 12 – The African Union (AU) will push for reforms to the global financial system, improved debt resolution mechanisms and stronger financial independence for the continent during the 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF)-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.
articles.takeaway: 12th Oct 2026 2 min read This photo taken on Feb.
body: 12th Oct 2026 2 min read This photo taken on Feb. 13, 2025 shows the buildings of the African Union (AU) Headquarters in Addis Ababa, capital of Ethiopia. (Xinhua/Michael Tewelde) NAIROBI, Kenya, Oct 12 – The African Union (AU) will push for reforms to the global financial system, improved debt resolution mechanisms and stronger financial independence for the continent during the 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF)-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

The meetings, scheduled for October 12-18, will provide a platform for the AU to advance Africa’s priorities on international tax cooperation, financial integration and access to resources for development.

The continental body said it would host four side events from October 13 to 16, focusing on international tax cooperation, operationalising African Union financial institutions, enabling instant cross-border payments and advancing effective debt resolution mechanisms.

“These discussions build on the AU’s ongoing work to reform the global financial architecture, strengthen Africa’s financial independence and unlock more resources for the continent’s development,” the organisation said.
The focus on debt resolution comes as African countries seek sustainable ways to manage debt obligations while financing infrastructure, public services and economic development.

More effective debt-resolution mechanisms could be part of broader efforts to address financing constraints facing developing economies. The AU will also use the meetings to advance discussions on international tax cooperation, an area central to efforts to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation and ensure African countries participate in shaping global tax rules.

articles.lead: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has publicly criticized President William Ruto's proposal to import buffaloes from India to address Kenya's milk shortage. Gachagua dismissed the plan, questioning the viability of buffaloes as a milk source and suggesting the government should instead focus on supporting and expanding the country's existing dairy cow population.
articles.takeaway: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua questions President William Ruto's plan to import buffaloes for milk, advocating for support of existing dairy farmers instead.
body: Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has publicly criticized President William Ruto's proposal to import buffaloes from India to address Kenya's milk shortage. Gachagua dismissed the plan, questioning the viability of buffaloes as a milk source and suggesting the government should instead focus on supporting and expanding the country's existing dairy cow population.

President Ruto had suggested exploring buffalo and camel breeds to diversify milk supply, citing potential for higher milk yields from buffaloes and increased market prices for camel milk. He reportedly instructed the Livestock Development Principal Secretary to investigate sourcing these animals.

The President's proposal comes amid a reported decline in milk deliveries to formal processors in July 2026 and rising market prices, attributed to dry conditions affecting pasture and increasing feed costs.

While the domesticated water buffalo was declared a food animal in January 2025, this did not establish a commercial dairy industry or authorize unrestricted importation. articles.headline: EPRA Announces Increased Electricity Costs for October
articles.dek: Consumers will face higher electricity bills due to new fuel energy, foreign exchange, and water resource management charges announced by the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority.
articles.lead: Electricity consumers in Kenya will see an increase in their bills starting in October, as the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has announced new monthly adjustments. These adjustments include a fuel energy charge of Sh3.22 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), a foreign exchange fluctuation charge of 87 cents per unit, and a water resource management levy of 1.34 cents per kWh.
articles.takeaway: Consumers will face higher electricity bills due to new fuel energy, foreign exchange, and water resource management charges announced by the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority.
body: Electricity consumers in Kenya will see an increase in their bills starting in October, as the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has announced new monthly adjustments. These adjustments include a fuel energy charge of Sh3.22 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), a foreign exchange fluctuation charge of 87 cents per unit, and a water resource management levy of 1.34 cents per kWh.

The combined additional charges will amount to approximately Sh4.10 per unit consumed. The foreign exchange adjustment will be applied to meter readings taken in September, while the fuel energy cost and water resource management levy will affect October readings. These changes will impact both households and businesses, increasing the cost of electricity purchased through prepaid tokens and postpaid billing.

The fuel energy cost reflects the expenses associated with electricity generated by thermal power plants and imported power, making it sensitive to fuel price fluctuations. The water resource management levy is intended to cover the costs of managing water resources used in hydropower generation. In September, Kenya purchased about 304.82 million kWh of electricity from hydropower plants.

The foreign exchange adjustment accounts for changes in the cost of electricity generation and supply due to currency exchange rate movements. Power purchase agreements and other electricity-related costs are often denominated in foreign currencies, such as the US dollar, meaning fluctuations in the Kenyan shilling can affect supplier costs and are passed on to consumers.

While individual levies may seem small, their cumulative effect raises the cost of each unit of electricity. Households that consume more electricity will experience larger increases in their monthly bills, and businesses with high electricity demand will face higher operating costs. EPRA continues to implement these monthly adjustments to account for various factors affecting electricity tariffs.

This initiative aims to conserve these endangered species while providing farmers with a new source of income and contributing to economic growth.

Mpingo trees are highly valued for their use in musical instruments and cultural items. Their durable hardwood is sought after globally, particularly for woodwind instruments. Due to threats from illegal harvesting and unsustainable exploitation, KEFRI is encouraging farmers to grow Mpingo on their land as an alternative to relying on wild populations.

Sandalwood, prized for its aromatic properties used in the perfume and fragrance industry, is also part of the promotion. The global market for sandalwood is estimated at 25 billion Kenyan shillings. KEFRI is encouraging its cultivation to ensure a sustainable supply and offer farmers participation in this high-value market.

KEFRI Director Simon Choge highlighted the significant commercial potential, noting that a single mature Mpingo tree can retail for approximately 10,000 Kenyan shillings. He encouraged farmers, especially in areas like Baringo County and the Kerio Valley, to consider growing these trees to diversify their income.

The program seeks to link forest conservation with economic opportunities, demonstrating how valuable indigenous trees can support livelihoods when managed sustainably. By shifting towards farm-based cultivation, KEFRI aims to reduce pressure on wild trees and foster responsible production.

The association contends that the tax hike, introduced under the Finance Act, 2026, will significantly raise production costs for local businesses.

Effective July 1, 2026, the excise duty on imported industrial sugar rose from Sh7.50 to Sh40 per kilogram. KAM states this increase makes imported sugar a key input for many manufacturers, with combined taxes and levies now potentially reaching 90 percent of its cost, insurance, and freight (CIF) value.

KAM estimates the new duty could lead to an additional Sh6 billion in annual costs for manufacturers. The association warns this could result in a 50 percent drop in capacity utilization and put approximately 3,000 jobs at risk.

Furthermore, KAM argues the increased duty disadvantages Kenyan manufacturers compared to competitors in Uganda and Tanzania, where similar excise duties are not applied to industrial sugar. This situation adds pressure as Kenyan firms navigate input costs while competing within the East African Community.

The association is also questioning the process by which the tax increase was implemented, citing inadequate public participation. The High Court has certified the application as urgent and directed the respondents, including the State Law Office and the Kenya Revenue Authority, to file their responses within seven days.

body: Members of the National Assembly Committee on Delegated Legislation have raised concerns regarding proposed privileges and immunities for the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and the Ford Foundation. The corporation aims to attract approximately Sh260 billion in additional investment through its Nairobi operations, which could bolster infrastructure development and strengthen Nairobi's role as a regional financial hub. Mudavadi encouraged the committee to consider the broader economic implications of hosting such international financial institutions.

The committee was informed that the AFC would operate under a framework comparable to diplomatic missions, adhering to Kenyan laws. However, the scrutiny underscores Parliament's role in reviewing subsidiary legislation to ensure public interest and legal frameworks are protected. The deliberations occur as the government seeks to attract international capital, with lawmakers insisting on a balance between economic gains and accountability.

articles.dek: A U.S. report highlights Kenya's failure to take meaningful enforcement action against public officials and recruitment agencies allegedly involved in human trafficking, citing official complicity.
articles.lead: A recent United States report has flagged Kenya's lack of significant enforcement against public officials and recruitment agencies suspected of involvement in human trafficking. articles.takeaway: A U.S.
body: A recent United States report has flagged Kenya's lack of significant enforcement against public officials and recruitment agencies suspected of involvement in human trafficking. The 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report indicates that while Kenyan authorities investigated three Ministry of Labour officials for alleged bribery related to migrant worker trafficking, broader concerns of collusion between officials and recruitment networks persist.

The report found no reported action against recruitment agencies allegedly owned by government employees, with authorities often pursuing less severe offenses like registration violations. The U.S. report stated that corruption and official complicity in trafficking crimes significantly hindered law enforcement efforts over the past year.

Concerns have been raised regarding accountability within institutions responsible for regulating overseas recruitment and protecting Kenyans seeking employment abroad. Media reports cited in the assessment suggest that over 10 percent of Kenyan government officials have ownership stakes in private employment agencies, including those recruiting for overseas jobs, creating potential conflicts of interest.

Allegations also surfaced of criminal syndicates collaborating with law enforcement and immigration departments at borders and airports to move trafficking victims within and into Kenya. The report further detailed claims that some Kenyan embassy officials in Saudi Arabia demanded sexual favors or cash from women seeking assistance to escape abusive employers and return home.

These findings coincide with a decline in anti-trafficking prosecutions and convictions in Kenya. The country convicted six traffickers in 2025, a decrease from 21 in 2024, and prosecutions dropped from 44 to 14 cases. Despite these issues, Kenya maintained its Tier 2 ranking in the U.S. assessment, acknowledging significant anti-trafficking efforts but noting that minimum standards for eliminating the crime have not been fully met.

The report did credit Kenya with identifying more victims, repatriating citizens exploited in overseas online scam operations, and securing its first civil judgment against a fraudulent recruiter. However, persistent concerns about official complicity continue to impede law enforcement and victim identification, with protection services for adult survivors remaining limited.

articles.headline: Sportpesa League Season Commences After Court Delays
articles.dek: The 2026/2027 Sportpesa League season is scheduled to begin on Saturday, October 11th, following a delay of over a month due to ongoing court disputes.
articles.lead: The 2026/2027 Sportpesa League season will officially kick off on Saturday, October 11th. The season's start was postponed for more than a month because of protracted legal challenges.
articles.takeaway: The 2026/2027 Sportpesa League season is scheduled to begin on Saturday, October 11th, following a delay of over a month due to ongoing court disputes.
body: The 2026/2027 Sportpesa League season will officially kick off on Saturday, October 11th. The season's start was postponed for more than a month because of protracted legal challenges.

On Saturday, two matches are scheduled to open the season. Mathare United will play APS Bomet at the Police Sacco Stadium at 2 pm. In the second fixture, Posta Rangers will face Shabana at Wang’uru Stadium in Mwea.

Sunday will feature four matches. Tusker FC, the Super Cup and Mozzartbet Cup champions, will compete against Ulinzi Stars at the Ulinzi Complex. National Super League (NSL) runners-up 3K FC will start their season at home at the Moi Stadium in Embu against Mara Sugar.

Additionally on Sunday, NSL champions Migori Youth FC are set to play Police FC at Awendo Green Stadium. The day's fixtures will conclude with Nairobi United facing Kenya Commercial Bank. Mombasa United, who won their playoff against Kariobangi Sharks, will play Kakamega Homeboyz next Wednesday at Mbaraki Sports Ground. Defending champions Gor Mahia will play Muranga Seal at Nyayo Stadium on Tuesday, October 13th. AFC Leopards will play their round nine fixture against Bandari FC at Nyayo Stadium on Wednesday, October 14th.

attribution.originalTitle: The long-awaited 2026/2027 Sportpesa League starts today

faqs.answer: The 2026/2027 Sportpesa League season begins on Saturday, October 11th.

faqs.answer: The league's start was delayed by over a month due to prolonged court disputes.

body: 10th Oct 2026 2 min read President William Ruto with PS State Department for Medical Services Ministry of Health Ouma Oluga in Tranz Nzoia NAIROBI, Kenya Oct 10 – President William Ruto has taken a swipe at the state of healthcare in Trans Nzoia, joking that patients who go to a hospital locals call Shakahola do not return, as he promised to address delays in completing health facilities in the county.

Locals in Trans Nzoia County have nicknamed the Wamalwa Kijana Teaching and Referral Hospital as “Shakahola Hospital” due to a severe healthcare crisis. “Ati watu wanaenda huko one-way?” Ruto asked, drawing attention to complaints about the hospital’s condition during his visit to Endebess, Trans Nzoia County.

The President acknowledged that the county was facing challenges in its hospitals, admitting that the completion of a major health project had been delayed. He blamed what he described as political disagreements and promised to resolve the issues holding back development.

“But msijali… hii kisirani tutasort out,” he told residents, assuring them that Trans Nzoia would not be left behind in the government’s development plans. Ruto said the government had already allocated Sh240 million towards the Endebess hospital project, with another Sh100 million needed to complete the facility.
He directed his Principal Secretary to ensure the remaining work was finished by December, promising to return in January or February to officially open the hospital.

“I want that hospital completed by December,” he said. The President also announced Sh1.2 billion for the construction of a 20-kilometre road linking Emuhaka, Matumbei, Bwara and Posta, saying the government had set aside funds for eight other roads in Trans Nzoia.
